_doc: Chalmer, the fisherman on the pier with a bare hook, sitting where he can see the old bridge piers. Topics on the hub offer his quick facts (the catfish, the foam).

open.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Chalmer. Don't need a last name, the river don't use one. You fish?
Nothing bites in January but the cold. I come out anyhow. Wife says it's the one place she can't hear me.
You want the catfish story or the bird story. Everybody wants one or the other and I charge the same.
Both stories are polished. Let's see which one's got the wear on it.

passives.line: Rod's rigged and the hook's bare. He isn't fishing. He's sitting where he can see the old bridge piers.
He said 'charge'. He wants the company more than the quarter. Let him talk and he'll pay you.

static.line: He sits where he can see the piers. Ask what comes up between them at dusk.

options.text: The catfish. Nobody ever picks the catfish.
The bird story. In your own time.
A bare hook's not fishing. You're sitting where you can see the piers.
What does your wife think you're doing out here?

fail.line: Fishing. Same as I tell you. Go ask Opal, she'll tell you I fish. She sells me the minnows I don't use.

catfish.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Dewey! Nobody picks Dewey. Twenty years and you're the first.
I'll do you Dewey proper when the tank pump's off. Sit. Bucket's dry, mostly.

bird.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: ...Everybody says 'bird' like I said bird. I never said bird.
I said two red lights on the water going upstream with no boat under 'em and no engine. That's all I said. The Register printed 'bird'.
Two lights and a current. That's an observation. 'Bird' was the newspaper's.

piers.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: ...Pier four. Ohio side. They left the old piers when they took the bridge down. Something sits on it at dusk, some days.
Sits like a man sits. I don't look direct. You look direct, it looks back, and then you're the one that's being fished.
Pier four at dusk. That's a stand. We can watch a stand.

piers_fail.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Bare hook's for the catfish I ain't caught yet. You don't know fishing, son.
Opal'll sell you a hook and a lecture. Get the lecture, it's better value.

wife.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Fishing. ...Thinking. She knows. She was on the Ohio side the day the bridge went, in line at the Kroger, and heard it go.
She don't come down to the river no more. Somebody in the family ought to. So I sit.

hub.speaker: rf_fisherman
hub.prompt: Pull up a bucket. Which one next.
lines: Pull up a bucket. Which one next.

options.text: Walk us out to the bridge approach at dusk, Chalmer. Show us pier four.
Lab says your foam's detergent and phosphate. Pump house, Thursdays. You were right.
Put a worm on it or admit you're keeping watch.

walk.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: ...Dusk. Not after. I'll show you where I stand, and you stand there, and I'll be back on this pier.
If it sits up, you don't wave at it. Dewey waved at it in '71. Dewey's in Columbus now and he don't fish.
I'll bring the receiver. If it's there, it'll be on the band before it's on the pier.

walk_fail.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: No. ...No, I'm sixty-one and I've done my looking.
Lyle on the Belle's got younger eyes and a ferry. Ask Lyle. He's pulled more out of this river than I've put in it.

foam.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Told you. Soap suds. Write it down, somebody in this town was right about something.
...Only thing is, the pumps ran Thursday and the foam glowed Wednesday too. First time in twenty years. Don't tell Opal, she'll frame it.

hook.speaker: rf_fisherman
lines: Dewey and me came down the morning after with grapples, like everybody. We brought up nothing we could keep. So I sit and watch the piers.
He's not watching for it. He's watching for them.
